newsitem.title: THAILAND: FOCUS-Thai, Malaysian phone firms see new role.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Thai, Malaysian phone firms see new role.

text.p: Thai and Malaysian phone companies on Monday signed a joint venture deal that they hope will open the way for the two firms to try to launch new forays into the regional telecommunications market.
The $260 million agreement signed by Samart Corporation Plc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd was the biggest business venture between Thailand and Malaysia.

"We hope that our partnership with Samart will enable us to accelerate the development of the new information technology and multimedia products so we can expand utilisation by customers and meet demand in Thailand, Malaysia and the region," Mohamed Said Bin Mohamed Ali, chief executive and executive director of Telekom Malaysia told reporters.
Telecommunications analysts said the deal was a trailblazer in that it could encourage more foreign phone firms to come to Thailand to acquire stakes in local firms in need of capital.
"We see more acquisitions for foreigners. Foreigners are very interested in buying Thai telecom firms especially the second-tier ones," said Paul Ngo, a telecommunication analyst at ING Baring.
"You will see ones that have financial troubles selling out (their shares)."

Under the agreement, Telekom Malaysia International (TMI), a wholly-owned unit of Telekom Malaysia, will buy 14 million shares, representing a 20.12 percent stake, in Samart Corp for a total of 1.86 billion baht ($71.5 million).
TMI will also invest 3.51 billion baht to purchase 98.8 million new shares, or a 33.3 percent holding, in Digital Phone Co Ltd (DPC), Samart's mobile phone unit.
TMI also agreed to infuse 1.17 billion baht in exchange for 32.9 million new shares of DPC by mid-March next year.

"We chose Telekom Malaysia to be our strategic partner, having searched several months from a number of well known international telecommunications entities," Charoenrath Vilailuck, Samart's executive chairman said.

"In addition to its strong customer-driven experience and business performance, Telecom Malaysia shares the same vision as Samart in spearheading the new convergent industry of computers, telecommunications and media."
Mohamed Ali said Malaysia Telekom's investment decision in Samart and its unit had been made after careful study and taking Thailand's economic slowdown into account.

"I don't think we have any concern about the (economic) situation here. Of course, we have studied the situation very carefully and we have decided to put money in and we know what we are putting our money in," Mohamed Ali said.
